assumptions.status: design-stage planning arithmetic under stated assumptions; not a result
assumptions.pass_rate_distribution: per-problem pass probability p_i ~ Beta(0.6, 0.5), shared across models; samples y_ij ~ Bernoulli(p_i), independent across models given p_i; a new problem set is drawn each replicate
assumptions.z: z_i = standardized logit(p_i) (p clipped to [1e-3, 1-1e-3]; standardized over the simulated problem set)
assumptions.score_model: s_P = d_P*y + a_P*z_i + e_P; s_S = d_S(level)*y + a_S*z_i + e_S; e ~ N(0,1); corr(e_P, e_S) = 0.5

difficulty_loadings.note: a_P > a_S: probe captures difficulty, inflating pooled AUROC; values are assumptions

assumptions.probe_within_auroc: 0.72, d_P = sqrt(2)*Phi^-1(0.72), before heterogeneity, clipping, and shocks
assumptions.zero_shot_stated: d0 = sqrt(2)*Phi^-1(0.60) (within AUROC about 0.60 before 11-bin rounding)
assumptions.trained_stated: d1 is calibrated per (k, true R) by bisection on a 30000-problem simulation so that the population residual R (all toggles on) equals the scenario value; calibration results are in the calibration block
assumptions.problem_heterogeneity: per-problem separation shift het ~ N(0, 0.3^2), shared by both readouts; separation clipped at 0
assumptions.gap_shocks: per-model, per-problem shock on the probe separation, SD 0.05 AUROC units / 0.26 (dA/dd near 0.26), independent across models, added to d_P
assumptions.stated_ties: stated score rounded to 11 bins: bin = round(10*sigmoid(s_S)), integers 0..10
assumptions.RECAL: isotonic (PAV, weighted by bin counts) of the active label on the stated bin, cross-fit: fit on even-index problems and apply to odd-index problems, and vice versa; empty bins forward-filled; probe unchanged; effect only through merged ties and cross-half value differences in the pooled metric
assumptions.TRAIN: stated separation d0 (off) versus d1 (on); the probe is the same in both
assumptions.DIFF: off = pooled AUROC over all samples of all problems (ties half); on = pair-weighted within-problem AUROC (sum of correct pass-fail pairs over sum of pairs; all-pass and all-fail problems carry zero pairs)
assumptions.LABEL: off = original weak suite label y_w; on = EvalPlus label y (true). Signals always relate to y
assumptions.weak_suite_false_passes: fraction f = 0.08 of truly failing samples (in expectation) become false passes in the weak suite; per-problem rate q_i = min(1, c*w_i), w_i = exp(-0.5*((p_i-0.5)/0.15)^2), c set so the expected failing-sample false-pass fraction is f
assumptions.multi_model: M models share the problem set; primary statistic is the mean over models of R; the bootstrap resamples problems jointly across models (paired, clustered)
assumptions.bootstrap: problem-clustered percentile bootstrap, B = 400 draws (B = 10000 in the study); pooled AUROC in the bootstrap is computed from counts, with the probe discretized into 128 quantile bins (negligible tie error); within metrics are exact
assumptions.decisions: equivalence (TOST): 90 percent percentile CI of R inside (-delta, delta), i.e. 5th percentile > -delta and 95th percentile < delta; superiority: 5th percentile of R > delta (one-sided 95 percent lower bound); else inconclusive; also P(5th percentile > 0)
assumptions.shapley: exact over 4 players and 16 cells (24 orderings); sequential decompositions in orders RECAL,TRAIN,DIFF,LABEL and the reverse; CI half-width = half of the 2.5-97.5 percentile range of the bootstrap draws, averaged over replicates
assumptions.monte_carlo_error: with 200 replicates the SE of a probability near 0.8 is about 0.028
